results.content:
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Most AI video tools still feel like editors with an AI button bolted on. You type a prompt, receive a rough draft, then spend an hour dragging clips around a timeline. CutBay takes a different approach: you describe what you want, provide source material, and chat with the AI to refine the result.

CutBay is built by the team behind FlexClip and positions itself as an AI video agent rather than a conventional video editor. Its core promise is simple: turn “anything” — an idea, blog post, Amazon product URL, PDF, spreadsheet, or folder of clips — into a share-ready video.

This review explains how CutBay works, what it does well, where it needs improvement, who should use it, and how it compares with FlexClip and other AI video tools. [...] Creative control may feel limited: Chat-based editing is fast, but advanced editors may miss precise timeline control.
 AI visuals need review: Stock assets and AI-generated images can look generic if you do not provide brand assets.
 Voiceover quality varies by language and script: Test pronunciation, pacing, and tone before publishing.
 Source-page extraction is not perfect: Product URLs, landing pages, and articles may contain layout elements or claims that need correction.
 Brand consistency requires setup: Upload logos, fonts, colors, and approved messaging rather than relying entirely on AI choices.
 Long-form videos need more oversight: The longer the video, the more important structure, pacing, and narrative flow become. [...] 6. Generate the first draft. Let CutBay create the structure, visuals, captions, and narration.
7. Review every claim. Check product specifications, pricing, shipping claims, guarantees, and customer-review language.
8. Refine by chat. Ask for a stronger hook, shorter runtime, clearer CTA, different music, or a new scene order.
9. Create platform variations. Produce a 15-second TikTok version, a 30-second Reel, and a longer YouTube or landing-page version.
10. Publish and measure. Track hook rate, watch time, clicks, add-to-carts, and cost per result. Use performance data to improve the next prompt.

results.content:
### Worth Keeping in Mind

CutBay is brand new, so independent reviews are still thin on the ground. It makes sense to try it on a real project before building a workflow around it.

As with any AI tool, give the result a once-over before you publish. Check the script, numbers, captions and tone of voice. The canvas editor is there for exactly that.

On pricing, the site invites you to start for free, but the details of the free and paid plans weren’t visible when we looked. Check cutbay.ai/pricing before you commit. The interface is also in English, so if you plan to make videos in other languages, test a short sample first.

### The Verdict [...] ### The Verdict

CutBay’s pitch is refreshingly simple: video should start with an idea, not with software. It takes in the content you already have, builds a full first draft, and lets you refine it by chat or by hand. If you create videos for marketing, teaching or business communication, it’s well worth a spin, and the free start makes that easy.

### FAQ

What is CutBay.ai?  
It’s an AI video agent that turns ideas, documents, links and media files into finished videos, and lets you edit them through chat.

Do I need video editing experience?
